Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the intro last week. Aegis is kicking off a light CAIQ review as part of our vendor assurance program — we'd like to schedule a 45-60 minute walkthrough with your security/product team to step through the CAIQ matrix and clarify a few items around logging, encryption in transit, and support for restricted regions.

Specific asks from our side:
- A short demo of where logs are stored and how long retained (we'll need a sample export)
- Clarification on key management (KMS/HSM integrations)
- SOC 2 scope and date of last report
- A list of owners we can call out for follow-up evidence

Are you available next week? Our preferred windows (PST): Tue 6/17 10:00–12:00, Wed 6/18 13:00–15:00. If those don't work we'll propose alternatives.

Also: procurement will need a copy of your standard SOC 2 summary and any data residency docs.

Thanks,
Samantha Holt
Vendor Assurance Lead
Aegis Systems

Samantha — quick notes from an engineering/evidence perspective before the call so we can be efficient:

- Log samples: we can provide 7 days of anonymized request/response logs + an activity audit stream. Format: gzipped JSON lines. We will scrub PII and present a redaction summary.
- Retention: default 90 days for hot logs; archive to S3 (encrypted SSE-KMS) for 3 years — we can provide export keys and a sample manifest.
- KMS: we support customer-managed CMKs via AWS KMS and can furnish a diagram and owner contact.
- SOC 2: Redwood's last Type II is March 2024; summary PDF attached. Full report requires an NDA and procurement process (we routinely provide it during contracting).

Action items for the call (we'll bring these):
- Walk through CAIQ Q1–Q30 (priority list from Aegis sheet)
- Share where in our architecture each item maps (owner + doc link)
- Agree evidence delivery windows (we suggest initial pass of documents within 5 business days post-call; higher-sensitivity items may take 10–15 days)

Small ask: please confirm whether your auditors need the raw manifest or a redacted sample only. That determines our scrub workflow.

Thanks — Kim
Kimberly Park
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SOC2-Redwood-2024-summary.pdf)
